key_history.title: Roanoke Island and the English colonial expeditions
key_history.summary: Roanoke Island was the site of English voyages and settlement attempts in the 1580s. The 1587 group led by John White remained on the island after its planned journey to the Chesapeake did not proceed. White returned in 1590 and found the settlement no longer present; the colonists' fate remains unresolved.
key_history.source_name: National Park Service — Fort Raleigh National Historic Site

key_history.title: Roanoke Island Freedmen's Colony
key_history.summary: After Union forces took Roanoke Island in February 1862, freedom seekers arrived and a community developed. The colony included homes, churches, schools, and other institutions. The federal government restored confiscated land after the war, and the colony was officially decommissioned by 1867. Its history is part of the island's story beyond the earlier English expeditions.
key_history.source_name: National Park Service — The Freedmen's Colony on Roanoke Island
